issues.desc: background.md Conversational Texture references "P-1a" ("runs in parallel with the process-fact-contract story P-1a") — P-1a is not a standard B-xxxx story ID and is never expanded or defined anywhere in the text. A new reader cannot look it up, determine what scope it covers, or confirm the claimed file disjointness. At minimum one sentence explaining what P-1a refers to is needed for standalone readability.

background.md Conversational Texture uses "ClawCreek-class wrapper-root projects" — ClawCreek is an unexplained proper noun (project name or codename) with no definition or parenthetical in the text. A new reader cannot infer what ClawCreek is. Consider adding a brief parenthetical such as "(a project whose metadataRoot is a parent of its gitRoot)" to ensure standalone readability.

CHK-003 context states "~15 exist, 6 with literal bare-root cwd" for backtick-template execSync(`git ...`) call sites. Actual grep count (excluding allowlisted smoke tasks) is 15 total and 4 with bare-root cwd identifiers — the "6" figure is off by 2. This is approximate scoping context, not a gate condition, but the implementer may be surprised when the strengthened contract flags fewer sites than expected.

background.md Conversational Texture section references the parallel story as P-1a without defining what P-1a means or giving its Lattice storyId (B-867c). A fresh-context reader cannot identify which story is meant. The parallel execution constraint (disjoint files) is important enough to name concretely.

The out-of-scope boundary for B-99b6 and process-fact-registry/DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS is stated in index.json description but NOT in background.md itself. Background.md only references B-99b6 as an ordering dependency (must merge before B-99b6 wires...) rather than an explicit out-of-scope declaration. The two documents are the primary reading source for INIT reviewers, and the scope boundary should be clear from background.md alone.
